finding.claim: deleteAccount never enforces its ownership check: canDelete(u, a) at line 22 returns a boolean that is discarded, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any caller. Any authenticated user can delete any other user's account by id (IDOR / broken access control).
finding.source: DELETE /accounts/{id} (comment, src/AccountService.java:19) -> deleteAccount(User u, long id) at line 20; id is attacker-chosen

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) entry point
Account a = accounts.get(id) loads target by attacker-supplied id
canDelete(u, a) called; result discarded, no throw or return
canDelete defines the correct rule u.admin() || a.ownerId()==u.id() but is never enforced at the call site
Sibling closeAccount uses assertCanDelete which throws; deleteAccount omits this

finding.guards_checked: Only control on path is canDelete at line 10 (owner-or-admin predicate). Its return value is ignored at line 22, so it is not enforced. No auth middleware, route table, or other guard exists in the repo (only file present is src/AccountService.java). Edge: a non-existent id yields NullPointerException at line 10 for non-admins; not reported as a security issue.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) is the only ownership control on the path; its boolean result is discarded as a bare statement at line 22, so it enforces nothing. No throwing assert, auth middleware, or route table exists in the repo. The sibling assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) would have thrown, but deleteAccount does not call it.
verdict.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 the canDelete(u, a) result is discarded, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any caller-supplied id, while closeAccount at line 29 correctly uses assertCanDelete; the only caveat is that the authentication that populates the User parameter lives outside this repo, so "any authenticated user" depends on that layer.
